title: test_heldout_reword_is_refused_at_the_gate adds about 8.5 s to the full tests.py run, over the 20 s darwin ceiling
goal: A whole-suite python3 _tools/tests.py run on the darwin host finishes within the 20 s ceiling of _tools/tests_ceiling.json, the ceiling unchanged (operator decision D-7zbgyagn). Cause, measured 2026-10-10 on an idle host at origin/main: the suite takes 14.3 s with -k 'not heldout_reword' (83 tests) and 22.8 s whole (85 tests); _tools/test_sync_e2e.py::test_heldout_reword_is_refused_at_the_gate, added by ST-wjm2ipaf, takes 8.9 s alone, since it runs the whole sync gate twice (a refused push, then a landing push after the row is replaced). Make that test cheaper while it still proves the sync gate refuses a reworded held-out row with exit 1, a REWORD line and origin/main unmoved, and keep its name, which ST-wjm2ipaf's check selects with -k heldout_reword.
notes: Moved into SP-5x5ut5ko by the orchestrator at the sprint review (2026-10-10): the review story's tests.py check fails on it, so the sprint cannot close without it. The worker that filed it measured under parallel-worker load and named host load; the idle-host runs above show the cause. Raising the ceiling is an operator decision and was not taken (conservative choice under the operator's delegated policy).
